source_text: Ita enim omnibus generaliter, edocente natura, inculcatum est, Deum iustum esse, ut manifestum sit, Deum non esse quem constiterit iustum non esse. Potest igitur et homo iustus esse; Deus vero esse nisi iustus non potest.
pass_a_gloss: For it has been so impressed on all generally, nature teaching, that God is just, that it is manifest that he is not God whom it has stood as not being just. A human therefore can also be just; but God cannot be unless just.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Nature's own teaching has impressed on everyone, without exception, that God is just. It is therefore clear that anyone proved not to be just is not God. A human being can be just; God cannot be anything but just.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
